guide.en:
# When a concept becomes unreadable

Suppose a model answers “What colour is the fourth planet from the Sun?” A two-step route is **Mars → red**. A lens turns an internal state into scores for words. If it recovers Mars at one depth but misses it later, did the concept disappear, or did the measurement stop working?

The [original J-lens study](https://transformer-circuits.pub/2026/workspace/) proposes a vocabulary-linked way to inspect part of a model’s internal representations. **Recovering a word and showing that the model uses its information are different claims.**

## Follow two research branches

**Readout methods:** [R-lens](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/nv8oedrnLXKRzNEL9/r-lens-making-j-lens-more-faithful-on-early-layers) changes the backward pass; [J++ Lens](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/nc9dHfcB22JdMzGbr/j-lens-jacobian-filtering-enables-more-faithful-workspace) adds filtering. Better scores motivate asking what each evaluation rewards.

**Model architecture:** a looped model reuses blocks. The [Ouro repository report](https://github.com/VykosMolt/JLens-Ouro) compares lenses aimed at a pass’s own exit with lenses aimed at the final exit. Changing that endpoint changes the reported recovery on the same confirmation states. This is a reported measurement result, not an Observatory reproduction.

## Read one curve carefully

The source reports own-exit minus final-target contrasts of **22.60, 26.50 and 34.17 percentage points** in passes 1–3, at physical blocks 26–37. Try can subtract the first mean from the last. That arithmetic describes three rounded aggregates; it cannot produce a confidence interval or tell us why the gap changes. Another published series uses a different estimator family and cannot be added to this contrast.

## Turn the observation into a question

After matching remaining computation distance, calibration budget and independently measured concept strength, does source pass or target exit still affect recoverability? Investigate compares transport limits, representation changes and overwritten or rebuilt content. The proposal is editable and exportable, with explicit controls, outcome criteria and missing resources. **No model experiment has been run here.**

The graph separates direct citations, method adaptation, evaluation, objections and editorial reading links. Evidence links and saved hypothesis revisions have their own meanings. Five branches remain visible; causal evidence, monitoring and the meaning of J-space still have incomplete coverage.
guide.zh:
# 当一个概念变得读不出来

假设模型回答“太阳系第四颗行星是什么颜色？”一个两步过程是 **火星 → 红色**。Lens 把内部状态转为词语分数。如果它在某个深度读到了火星，后来却读不到，是概念消失了，还是测量失效了？

[原始 J-lens 研究](https://transformer-circuits.pub/2026/workspace/)提出一种与词表关联的方法，观察模型内部表示的一部分。**读到一个词，与证明模型使用了对应信息，是不同主张。**

## 先沿两条分支看

**读出方法：**[R-lens](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/nv8oedrnLXKRzNEL9/r-lens-making-j-lens-more-faithful-on-early-layers)修改反向传播；[J++ Lens](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/nc9dHfcB22JdMzGbr/j-lens-jacobian-filtering-enables-more-faithful-workspace)加入筛选。分数提高后，还要问评估究竟奖励了什么。

**模型结构：**循环模型重复使用相同块。[Ouro 仓库报告](https://github.com/VykosMolt/JLens-Ouro)比较以当前轮出口及最终出口为目标的 lens。在同一确认集状态上，改变目标出口会改变报告的恢复能力。这是来源的测量报告，并非本站复现。

## 仔细读一条曲线

来源报告，在物理块 26–37、第 1–3 轮，本轮出口减最终终点的差值为 **22.60、26.50、34.17 个百分点**。Try 可以用最后一个均值减去第一个。这只是三个取整汇总值的算术，不能生成置信区间，也不能解释差距变化的原因。另一个报告序列来自不同估计器族，不能与这组差值相加。

## 把观察变成问题

匹配剩余计算距离、校准预算及独立测得的概念强度后，源轮次或目标出口是否仍影响可恢复性？Investigate 比较传输受限、表示变化，以及内容被覆盖或重建等竞争解释。提案可编辑、保存和导出，包含对照、结果判据和缺失资源。**本站尚未运行模型实验。**

# When a workspace becomes unreadable

*Research guide · 22 October 2026 · approximately 10 minutes, with optional deeper paths*

Suppose a model answers a two-hop question: identify a planet, then report its colour. A lens reads the intermediate concept at one depth, loses it, and finds it again later. What happened during the gap? The concept might have disappeared. It might also have moved into a representation that this lens cannot read.

That ambiguity connects much of the discussion around J-lens. My synthesis is that **workspace visibility should be treated as a measurement with conditions attached: the method, the state being inspected, and the endpoint it reads toward.** Whether the recovered information drives a computation or helps a monitor requires additional evidence.

This is a selective map of five connected debates, including substantive comments beneath the papers. The interactive atlas contains 20 traceable entries across 14 source documents. It distinguishes reported findings, objections, author responses and untested proposals. Connections between works are editorial synthesis unless explicitly marked as a direct reply.

<!-- ATLAS -->

## Start here: what does a lens measure?

A model's **internal state** is a collection of numbers produced as it processes an input. A **readout** turns some of those numbers into an interpretable output, such as scores for words. A **lens** is the method used to obtain that readout. Different lenses can give different answers about the same state.

In the [original J-lens study](https://transformer-circuits.pub/2026/workspace/), **workspace** refers to a proposed shared representational space involved in reporting, modulation and flexible computation. The measured J-space approximates it. A readable word is evidence about the measurement; showing that the model uses the corresponding information calls for further tests.

Keep the planet example in mind: “the lens recovered *Mars*” and “the model used its representation of Mars to answer *red*” are different claims. This guide follows what evidence could connect them. You can then use the lab to check reported numbers and frame a next test; its calculations do not rerun the model.

## 1. What is getting better when a lens improves?

The original [J-lens paper](https://transformer-circuits.pub/2026/workspace/) constructs vocabulary-linked readouts from averaged Jacobians and tests reporting, modulation and flexible computation. These functional claims make the work more interesting than a collection of plausible-looking token lists. But the measured J-space remains an approximation to the proposed workspace.

[R-lens](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/nv8oedrnLXKRzNEL9/r-lens-making-j-lens-more-faithful-on-early-layers) changes backward propagation using layer-wise relevance rules and improves early readouts in several tested models. [J++](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/nc9dHfcB22JdMzGbr/j-lens-jacobian-filtering-enables-more-faithful-workspace) combines relevance propagation, clustered and weighted Jacobians, and vocabulary filtering, with improvements across six open models. This is real methodological progress, but “better” depends on the evaluation.

Two comments sharpen that qualification. [StellaAthena asks](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/nv8oedrnLXKRzNEL9/r-lens-making-j-lens-more-faithful-on-early-layers?commentId=tx8tp7PwFNcP4BvPh) whether a score can reward anticipating a later layer rather than describing the current one. [Niranjan Deshpande asks](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/nc9dHfcB22JdMzGbr/j-lens-jacobian-filtering-enables-more-faithful-workspace?commentId=YhfAKjBSL3ZkreasB) whether filtering gains transfer to audits without a specified target word. These are evaluation challenges, not demonstrated failures of the methods.

For a follow-up, I would separate three outcomes: recovering a known intermediate, describing a state faithfully, and discovering an unexpected concern. The first gives a clean development target. The third is closer to the audit use case. Improvement on one should motivate testing the others, rather than silently stand in for them.

## 2. Architecture changes what the measurement means

The [looped-transformer preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01924) compares Ouro and Huginn. It reports repeated reconstruction of workspace content in Ouro, while Huginn preserves content beyond the lens's effective transport window. This makes a crucial distinction: the lifetime of information and the distance over which a particular readout works can differ.

A separate [Ouro repository report](https://github.com/VykosMolt/JLens-Ouro) finds stronger early-pass recovery when a lens targets that pass's own exit rather than the final exit. Its own-exit comparison is a post-confirmation analysis, and it lacks a tuned-lens baseline and a causal-use result. It is useful corroborating motivation for an endpoint experiment, with those limits attached.

The [Mamba study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.32102) adds another variable: the state carrier. Residual-stream and recurrent-state readouts recover complementary information; better verbal access does not consistently yield better relational answers. A residual-only comparison can therefore miss information available elsewhere in the architecture.

My inference is that an architecture survey needs a more explicit unit of comparison than “the model has a workspace.” Specify the checkpoint, computation depth, state carrier, token position, lens, and readout endpoint. Otherwise an apparent architectural difference may partly reflect a difference in measurement difficulty. This is especially relevant when one model reuses weights across many computational steps.

## 3. Readability and causal use need separate scoreboards

[WorkspaceBench](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/Zeg2JztbdhguL48uH/workspacebench-evaluating-interpretability-methods-for-the) provides 3,356 questions across 27 families, including recovery and hallucination evaluations. In the comments, [Burny asks about interventions](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/Zeg2JztbdhguL48uH/workspacebench-evaluating-interpretability-methods-for-the?commentId=Foio2Goqoa6pFLPir); [Neel Nanda replies](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/Zeg2JztbdhguL48uH/workspacebench-evaluating-interpretability-methods-for-the?commentId=s5dLELdceTzSPPD37) that causal tests are less method-agnostic and outside this benchmark's scope. That is a useful boundary on what a benchmark score establishes.

[Mirella Zeisler's replication](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/pnDjvdo6cX2H7Ddsy/is-the-j-space-a-global-workspace-for-multi-hop-reasoning-an) directly investigates interventions. Across two models and two prompt banks, direct-answer swaps outperform intermediate swaps in three of four settings. This narrows the causal interpretation of those settings without ruling out every proposed workspace function.

I would therefore report recovery and intervention results side by side. A readable intermediate might be causally important, redundant, or correlated with a computation elsewhere. Conversely, a weak edit can reflect a poor intervention rather than an unused concept. Controls must test edit strength, specificity and general disruption before either positive or negative results support a broad claim.

## 4. Monitoring depends on where and when you look

[Neel Nanda's review](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/zFJ3ZdQwrTWE9jT5S/a-review-of-anthropic-s-global-workspace-paper) separates the paper's scientific, methodological, practical and philosophical claims. That separation helps interpret two recent monitoring reports that could otherwise look contradictory.

[Jimmy Liu reports](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/bhvaAbSPZgiG3oJPu/on-qwen-the-j-lens-readouts-at-the-newline-token-reveal-lies-4) a deception-related signal at a post-response newline in Qwen3.6-27B, with poor transfer to the other tested models. A trained probe performs better. This is a retrospective signal, so the result alone does not establish warning before an action.

[Daniel Huber's small planted-error experiment](https://www.agent-engineering.ch/experiments/jacobian-lens/) finds no added value over output surprise at one layer of Gemma 4 12B. It uses 30 error/neutral pairs and development-only analysis; per-pair records are unavailable. It also does not test anticipation of the model's own future mistakes.

These studies vary in model, task, token position, layer and baseline. My inference is that neither supports a general verdict on J-lens monitoring. A useful comparison should ask what information becomes available, how early, and whether it changes a decision beyond what outputs or a trained probe already provide. [Discussion of hidden serial computation](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/PLisnSFir8y5AHkmP/how-concerned-should-we-be-about-astra-s-recurrent) motivates that question, but does not itself validate a monitoring method.

## 5. What does the word workspace commit us to?

The [Eleos commentary](https://eleosai.org/papers/eleos_gwt_commentary_20260706.pdf#page=6) distinguishes vocabulary directions from the concepts a workspace might contain, and accessible representations from an integrated stream. Functional access and phenomenal consciousness are separate claims.

[Jayrup's frequency analysis](https://jayrup.me/blog/jacobian-lens-frequency) supplies a narrower measurement concern: token frequency affects vector-norm rankings in small-model tests. It does not refute the original large-model capacity claim. The original paper's [Template and Oracle extensions](https://transformer-circuits.pub/2026/workspace/) also move beyond single-token descriptions, while introducing their own costs and reliability questions.

My takeaway is to keep the operational definition visible. A token-based readout can be useful even when tokens are an imperfect description of concepts. But changing the vocabulary or the decoder may change what appears to occupy the space. Claims about a common mechanism need evidence that survives reasonable changes in this measuring apparatus.

## A small experiment worth doing next

Our first worked investigation asks: **how much apparent loss of an intermediate in Ouro is explained by the readout endpoint?** This section is a proposal; no new experiment has been run for this guide.

Start with one frozen Ouro checkpoint and a two-hop task with known intermediates. Split by intermediate concept before fitting lenses or selecting layers. Cache the same activations for every comparison, and choose the primary metric and selection procedure before opening the held-out set.

Compare own-exit and final-exit readouts on those identical states. Use equal fitting budgets for J-lens and R-lens; include a logit lens and a tuned linear readout as baselines. Plot held-out recovery against computational distance to the chosen endpoint. Report paired uncertainty clustered by concept, so paraphrases of one fact do not masquerade as independent evidence.

Endpoint and transport distance are coupled in this design. To investigate that confound, compare matched distances where possible and add a depth-matched untied baseline. If the available compute cannot support those controls, report an endpoint association and leave the mechanism unresolved.

Then choose one layer using the development split and test an intermediate swap on held-out examples. Include direct-answer swaps, unrelated-concept edits, matched-norm random directions and output-disruption checks. This second stage asks a different question from recovery and should retain a separate result panel.

There are useful outcomes even without a new method. Better own-exit recovery on identical states would show that unreadability depends on the measurement. An effect that disappears after distance controls would favour a transport explanation. A specific intermediate edit that predictably changes a downstream answer would add causal evidence. Failure to recover or edit the concept would leave several possibilities open; it would not by itself establish absence.

The contribution I would aim for is a precise statement of **when a readout stops being informative**, with enough controls to explain at least one failure mode. That gives architecture comparisons and monitoring experiments a firmer starting point.

---

*Research note: AI-assisted synthesis prepared for author review. Sources and selected comment threads checked on 21 October 2026. This is not an exhaustive survey or an independent replication. Reported findings, our interpretation and the proposed experiment are separated throughout. The atlas includes the additional Jacobian-alignment proposal and exact comment links.*

## Acknowledgments

The research and criticisms in this guide belong to the authors linked above and in the source ledger, including the individual commenters. The Ouro data are credited to VykosMolt; our plots and calculations use reported summaries, not a new reproduction.

[Lilian Weng](https://lilianweng.github.io/posts/2026-07-04-harness/) informs the explanatory organization, and [SafeLoop](https://safeloop-workshop.github.io/) informs the visual direction. [Paper2Agent](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11044-y), [DiscoveryRSI](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23839) and [autoresearch](https://github.com/karpathy/autoresearch) inform the research-tool design. References & acknowledgments on the companion website lists each design influence, related project and implementation credit, with its specific role. AI assisted the drafting and implementation; interpretations and errors here remain our responsibility.

# 当 workspace 变得读不出来

*研究导读 · 2026 年 10 月 22 日 · 入门约 10 分钟，可按需深入*

假设模型正在回答一道两跳问题：先确定是哪颗行星，再回答它的颜色。我们用 lens 在某一层读到了中间概念，往后几层却读不到，再往后又出现了。这段空白里发生了什么？概念可能消失了，也可能换了一种表示，让这副 lens 暂时读不出来。

这个歧义贯穿了不少 J-lens 后续讨论。我的理解是：**谈 workspace 是否可见时，需要同时说明读出方法、被观察的状态，以及读出所指向的终点。** 至于读出的信息是否参与计算、能否帮助监控模型，还需要另外的证据。

下面沿着五个问题梳理相关工作，也纳入论文评论区里有实质内容的讨论。交互图收录了 14 份来源中的 20 个条目，分别标明实验报告、质疑、作者回应和待验证的提议。除明确标注的直接回复外，图中的连接都是本文对工作之间关系的整理。

<!-- ATLAS -->

## 从这里开始：lens 到底在测什么？

模型处理输入时会产生一组组数字，这就是这里说的**内部状态**。**读出**把其中的信息转为更容易理解的输出，例如词语的分数；**lens** 是获得这种读出的方法。面对同一个状态，不同 lens 可能给出不同答案。

在[原始 J-lens 研究](https://transformer-circuits.pub/2026/workspace/)中，**workspace** 指一种被提出的共享表示空间，参与报告、调控和灵活计算。测得的 J-space 是它的近似。读到一个词提供的是有关测量的证据；要说明模型实际使用了对应信息，还需要进一步检验。

记住开头的行星例子：“lens 读到了火星”和“模型使用火星的表示回答红色”是两种不同主张。这份导读围绕能连接它们的证据展开。随后可以在实验室里检查报告数值、整理下一步检验；其中的计算不会重新运行模型。

## 1. 一副 lens 变好了，究竟是哪方面变好？

最初的 [J-lens 论文](https://transformer-circuits.pub/2026/workspace/)用平均 Jacobian 构建与词表关联的读出方向，并测试了报告、调控和灵活计算等功能。这些功能实验让它超出了“列出一些看起来合理的 token”的范围。不过，测得的 J-space 仍然只是所提出的 workspace 的一种近似。

[R-lens](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/nv8oedrnLXKRzNEL9/r-lens-making-j-lens-more-faithful-on-early-layers)用逐层相关性传播规则修改反向传播，在若干模型上改善了早层读出。[J++](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/nc9dHfcB22JdMzGbr/j-lens-jacobian-filtering-enables-more-faithful-workspace)结合相关性传播、Jacobian 聚类加权和词表筛选，在六个开放模型上取得了改进。这是方法上的进展，但“更好”仍取决于用什么来评估。

两条评论把这个问题说得更具体。[StellaAthena 问](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/nv8oedrnLXKRzNEL9/r-lens-making-j-lens-more-faithful-on-early-layers?commentId=tx8tp7PwFNcP4BvPh)：分数提高，会不会是因为读出提前预测了后面层的答案，而没有忠实描述当前层？[Niranjan Deshpande 问](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/nc9dHfcB22JdMzGbr/j-lens-jacobian-filtering-enables-more-faithful-workspace?commentId=YhfAKjBSL3ZkreasB)：没有预先指定目标词时，筛选带来的收益还能用于审计吗？这些是在质疑评估能支持多强的结论，目前不能当作方法已经失败的证据。

后续实验里，我会分别评估三件事：恢复一个已知的中间概念、忠实描述当前状态，以及发现预料之外的问题。第一项适合开发方法，第三项更接近实际审计。一项进步之后，值得接着测另外两项。

## 2. 模型结构会改变测量的含义

[Looped Transformer 预印本](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01924)比较了 Ouro 和 Huginn。作者报告，Ouro 在每轮 loop 中重建 workspace 内容；Huginn 的内容则可以持续存在，超过 lens 有效传递的范围。这提示我们：信息能保留多久，与某种读出能跨多远起作用，可以是两件事。

另一份 [Ouro 仓库报告](https://github.com/VykosMolt/JLens-Ouro)发现，把读出终点设在当前轮出口，比设在最终出口更容易恢复早期轮次的内容。不过，这项比较是在确认分析之后补做的，也缺少 tuned-lens 基线和内容被因果使用的结果。它为进一步做终点实验提供了动机，结论需要保留这些边界。

[Mamba 研究](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.32102)又引入了一个变量：信息存在哪里。残差流和递归状态中的读出能够恢复互补信息，但更容易用语言读出，并不总能带来更好的关系问答表现。只看残差流，可能漏掉架构中其他位置的信息。

因此，我认为架构比较需要比“这个模型有 workspace”更明确的单位：哪个 checkpoint、多少计算深度、哪类状态、哪个 token 位置、什么 lens，以及哪个读出终点。否则，看似来自架构的差异，可能有一部分来自测量难度。当模型在很多计算步骤中反复使用同一组权重时，这个问题尤其值得注意。

## 3. 读得出来，与参与计算，需要分别评估

[WorkspaceBench](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/Zeg2JztbdhguL48uH/workspacebench-evaluating-interpretability-methods-for-the)提供了 27 类、共 3,356 道问题，包含恢复和幻觉评估。评论区里，[Burny 问有没有干预实验](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/Zeg2JztbdhguL48uH/workspacebench-evaluating-interpretability-methods-for-the?commentId=Foio2Goqoa6pFLPir)；[Neel Nanda 回应](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/Zeg2JztbdhguL48uH/workspacebench-evaluating-interpretability-methods-for-the?commentId=s5dLELdceTzSPPD37)，因果实验更依赖具体方法，因此没有纳入这个 benchmark。知道这个范围，才能正确理解分数。

[Mirella Zeisler 的复现](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/pnDjvdo6cX2H7Ddsy/is-the-j-space-a-global-workspace-for-multi-hop-reasoning-an)直接研究了干预。在两个模型、两组 prompt 的四种设置中，有三种设置里直接替换答案比替换中间概念更有效。这限制了这些设置中的因果解释，但尚不能排除所有提出的 workspace 功能。

我会把恢复结果和干预结果并列展示。读得出的中间概念可能确实重要，也可能是冗余的，或者只是与别处的计算相关。反过来，编辑效果弱，也可能是干预方法不合适。要从结果推出更广的结论，还得检查编辑强度、特异性，以及它有没有普遍破坏模型输出。

## 4. 监控能否有用，取决于在哪里、什么时候看

[Neel Nanda 的评论](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/zFJ3ZdQwrTWE9jT5S/a-review-of-anthropic-s-global-workspace-paper)区分了论文的科学、方法、实际应用和哲学主张。沿用这个区分，有助于理解两份表面上可能相互冲突的监控报告。

[Jimmy Liu 报告](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/bhvaAbSPZgiG3oJPu/on-qwen-the-j-lens-readouts-at-the-newline-token-reveal-lies-4)，在 Qwen3.6-27B 回答后的换行位置，可以读到与欺骗有关的信号，但向其他被测模型的迁移较差，训练过的 probe 表现也更好。由于信号出现在回答之后，这个结果本身还不能说明能在行动前预警。

[Daniel Huber 的小规模植入错误实验](https://www.agent-engineering.ch/experiments/jacobian-lens/)在 Gemma 4 12B 的某一层上，没有发现 lens 相比输出惊讶度提供额外价值。实验用了 30 对错误／中性样本，只做了开发阶段分析，且未提供逐对记录。它也没有测试能否提前识别模型自己将要犯的错误。

这些研究的模型、任务、token 位置、层和基线都不同。我的判断是，目前任何一份都不足以对 J-lens 监控做出普遍裁决。更有用的比较是：获得了什么信息、多早能获得，以及它能否在输出或训练过的 probe 之外改变实际决策。[关于隐藏串行计算的讨论](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/PLisnSFir8y5AHkmP/how-concerned-should-we-be-about-astra-s-recurrent)说明了这个问题为什么值得关心，但它本身并未验证某种监控方法。

## 5. 使用 workspace 这个词，意味着什么？

[Eleos 的评论](https://eleosai.org/papers/eleos_gwt_commentary_20260706.pdf#page=6)区分了词表方向和 workspace 可能容纳的概念，也区分了可访问的表示与整合后的信息流。功能上的访问能力，与现象意识，是不同层面的主张。

[Jayrup 的词频分析](https://jayrup.me/blog/jacobian-lens-frequency)指出了更具体的测量问题：在所测的小模型中，token 频率影响向量范数的排名。这尚未推翻原论文对大模型容量的主张。原论文中的 [Template 和 Oracle 扩展](https://transformer-circuits.pub/2026/workspace/)也在尝试超越单 token 描述，同时带来了新的成本与可靠性问题。

我认为需要一直把操作性定义放在读者眼前。即便 token 不能完美描述概念，基于 token 的读出仍然可以有用。不过，换词表或解码器，可能改变我们看到的空间内容。关于共同机制的主张，需要经得住测量工具的合理变化。

## 下一步，值得做的一个小实验

第一个调查示例是：**Ouro 中有多少看似丢失的中间概念，可以用读出终点来解释？** 这里提出的是实验方案，这份导读尚未运行新实验。

从一个冻结的 Ouro checkpoint 和中间概念已知的两跳任务开始。先按中间概念划分数据，再拟合 lens、选择层。所有比较使用同一份缓存激活；在查看留出集之前，确定主指标和选择流程。

在这些相同状态上，比较以本轮出口和最终出口为终点的读出。J-lens 和 R-lens 使用相同的拟合预算，并加入 logit lens 和经过训练的线性读出作为基线。画出留出集恢复率随到目标终点的计算距离变化的曲线。按概念聚类报告配对比较的不确定性，避免把同一事实的不同措辞当成独立证据。

这个设计里，终点和传递距离是耦合的。为了研究这个混杂因素，应该在可行时比较相同距离，并加入深度匹配、各层不共享权重的基线。如果算力不足以完成这些对照，就把结果限定为终点与恢复率之间的关联，暂时不解释机制。

接着，用开发集选一层，在留出样本上替换中间概念。对照包括直接替换答案、编辑无关概念、范数匹配的随机方向，以及输出受损程度的检查。这一步回答的问题与恢复率不同，结果也应单独展示。

即使没有提出新方法，几种结果仍然有价值：同一状态在本轮出口更容易读出，说明不可读性取决于测量；加入距离对照后效应消失，会更支持传递距离的解释；替换特定中间概念后，下游答案按预测改变，则增加了因果证据。如果既读不出也改不动，还存在多种可能，不能仅据此断言概念不存在。

我希望这项工作最后能明确回答：**一种读出在什么条件下不再提供有效信息？** 只要对照足够，能解释清楚一种失效原因，就能为架构比较和监控实验提供更扎实的起点。
